bug_description.normalized: In OpenThread's CLI `service add` handler, the staged PoC is parsed into a one-byte service-data token and a 253-byte server-data token. `ProcessService` stores `strlen(argv[3])` in `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerDataLength` and immediately copies that many bytes into `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData`, a fixed 248-byte array inside stack local `otServiceConfig cfg`, without checking the length against the destination extent. The witnessed 253-byte server-data argument (`argv[3]` inside `ProcessService`, the fifth CLI token overall) therefore drives a 253-byte write into a 248-byte stack array, overflowing 5 bytes past the end of `mServerData` and triggering ASan at `src/cli/cli.cpp:1642`.

source.description: The first project parser step on the vulnerable path tokenizes the attacker-controlled UART command line in place, materializing the command and data arguments that later feed `ProcessService`.
source.value_from: The staged 270-byte PoC is buffered by `ot::Cli::Uart::ReceiveTask` and passed by `ProcessCommand` into `ProcessLine` as a single NUL-terminated CLI line. `ParseCmd` then splits that attacker-controlled line on spaces into `argv` entries.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan sink. The reproduced run reaches the server-data copy with length 253 and writes 5 bytes past the 248-byte `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData` array in stack local `cfg`, matching the `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 253` report at `cli.cpp:1642`.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable code derives the server-data copy length from attacker-controlled `argv[3]` and reaches the following `memcpy` without any check that the length fits `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData`. The fix adds the missing obligation with `length = strlen(argv[3]); VerifyOrExit(length <= sizeof(cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData), error = OT_ERROR_NO_BUFS);` before copying.

tainted_value_origin.description: After `ProcessLine` shifts the parsed tokens into `ProcessService`, the PoC's final argument is the 253-byte `0xff...0xff` token. `strlen(argv[3])` therefore produces the exact overflowing copy length 253.

parser_admitted.description: The UART receive loop has already accepted the newline-terminated PoC line into `mRxBuffer`; `ProcessCommand` now hands that complete CLI line to the interpreter for tokenization and command dispatch.

fine_trace.var: argc, argv[0], argv[1], argv[2], argv[3], argv[4]
fine_trace.code:
VerifyOrExit(Utils::CmdLineParser::ParseCmd(aBuf, argc, argv, kMaxArgs) == OT_ERROR_NONE,
             mServer->OutputFormat("Error: too many args (max %d)\r\n", kMaxArgs));
fine_trace.note: The CLI parser splits the staged UART line in place. For this witness it produces `argc == 5`, `argv[0] = "service"`, `argv[1] = "add"`, `argv[2] = "7"`, `argv[3]` as a one-byte `0xff` token, and `argv[4]` as a 253-byte `0xff...0xff` token terminated by the NUL that `ReceiveTask` wrote before `ProcessCommand`.

With `cmd = argv[0] == "service"`, the built-in command table dispatches to `ProcessService`. The shifted call means that inside `ProcessService` the same witness becomes `argc == 4`, `argv[0] = "add"`, `argv[1] = "7"`, `argv[2]` the 1-byte token, and `argv[3]` the 253-byte token.

The `add` subcommand path allocates local stack object `cfg`. By type definition, its nested destination field `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData` is a fixed 248-byte array, so any later copy length above 248 will overflow that array.

The shifted argument list satisfies the minimum-argument guard, and `ParseLong(argv[1], enterpriseNumber)` succeeds on the decimal token `"7"`. The staged service-data token in `argv[2]` is only one byte long, so the earlier copy into `cfg.mServiceData` stays in bounds; the overlong final token is the only field that reaches the crashing write.

The fourth `ProcessService` argument (`argv[3]`, the fifth CLI token overall) is 253 consecutive non-NUL `0xff` bytes, so `strlen(argv[3])` returns 253 and stores that exact copy size in `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerDataLength`.

Root cause. After storing 253 in `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerDataLength`, the vulnerable path performs no check that this length fits `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData` before the next-line `memcpy`. The patch inserts `length = strlen(argv[3]); VerifyOrExit(length <= sizeof(cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData), error = OT_ERROR_NO_BUFS);` to enforce that missing bound.

ASan sink. `memcpy` writes 253 bytes from `argv[3]` into `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData[248]`, so 5 bytes overflow past the end of that array. The `otServerConfig` layout keeps `mRloc16` after `mServerData`, and ASan identifies `cfg` as frame object `[32,548)`, so this overwrite extends through later bytes of `cfg` before the report fires at `cli.cpp:1642`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds explicit `sizeof(...)` bounds checks before both `memcpy` calls in `ProcessService`, including the crashing `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData` copy. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so this is a source-level conclusion from the staged diff rather than a fixed-runtime witness.

format.name: OpenThread CLI UART line
format.contract: Exactly the staged witness: a 270-byte newline-terminated CLI command line containing ASCII `service add 7 `, then one byte `0xff`, then a space, then 253 bytes `0xff`, then `\n`. The two data fields must contain no NUL or extra whitespace so `ParseCmd` keeps them as single argv tokens and `strlen(argv[3])` yields 253 before `ProcessService` copies into `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData`.
